findings.current: Monsters and humans were sworn enemies, as ordained by the gods.
findings.defect: The draft changes the singular 신 into plural gods, altering a stated world fact.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly uses the singular subject 신이.
findings.replacement: Monsters and humans were sworn enemies, as ordained by God.
findings.source: 몬스터와 인간은 신이 정한 숙적의 관계다.

findings.current: “I’m saying I’ll laugh, so why the fuck do you care? Are you my senior or something?”
findings.defect: The generic “senior” loses 맞선임’s specifically military sense of the service member directly senior to the speaker, weakening the joke and Jin’s register.
findings.rationale: 맞선임 is a military-hierarchy term, not a generic senior person.
findings.replacement: “Why the fuck do you care if I laugh? What are you, my immediate senior in the army?”
findings.source: “내가 웃겠다는데 왜 지랄이야. 네가 내 맞선임이냐?”

findings.current:
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights trembled.

I was no different.
findings.defect: The second sentence grammatically suggests that Jin’s nonexistent eye-lights also trembled; the source means he was similarly shaken by the unexpected event.
findings.rationale: 그것은 나 역시 크게 다르지 않았다 compares their startled reactions, not their physical eye-lights.
findings.replacement:
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights trembled.

I was just as shaken.
findings.source: 아크 리치의 안광이 파르르 떨렸다. 그것은 나 역시 크게 다르지 않았다.

findings.current: Why had it chosen to become my shield even though it knew it would be erased?
findings.defect: The draft turns the Skeleton Warlord’s resolve to face possible Erasure into certain foreknowledge that it would be erased, and it does not use the established term Erasure.
findings.rationale: 소멸을 각오하다 means being resolved or prepared to face Erasure, not knowing with certainty that it will happen.
findings.replacement: Why had it chosen to become my shield even though it had been prepared to face Erasure?
findings.source: 어째서 소멸을 각오하면서까지 스스로 방패를 자처했느냐고.

findings.defect: The unestablished romanization “Golgoli” leaves the affectionate bone-based nickname opaque, while “our” is unnatural English address.
findings.rationale: 골골이 is an affectionate nickname for the skeleton; “Bones” conveys that function naturally without introducing an unexplained proper name.

findings.current: - All injuries and attributes have been restored!
findings.defect: Injuries cannot naturally be “restored”; they are healed, while attributes are restored.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves both recoveries while giving each object its natural English verb.
findings.replacement: - All injuries have been healed, and all attributes restored!

findings.current: The fire dragon spread its wings and soared from my dantian, transforming into a ball of flame as it surged through my four limbs and hundred bones.
findings.defect: “Four limbs and hundred bones” is a stiff literal calque of the idiom 사지 백해 rather than natural contemporary English.
findings.rationale: 사지 백해 denotes the whole body, especially every limb and bone, rather than a literal anatomical count.
findings.replacement: The fire dragon spread its wings and soared from my dantian, transforming into a ball of flame as it surged through every limb and bone in my body.
findings.source: 단전에서 날개를 펴고 날아오른 화룡이 불덩이가 되어 사지 백해로 솟구친다.

findings.current: The Arch Lich flung its hands about in a frenzy, but the magic it fired collided with the heat surrounding me like a barrier and vanished before it could even reach me.
findings.defect: The draft omits the Arch Lich flailing its feet as well as its hands, changing the described full-body action.
findings.rationale: 손발 explicitly includes both upper and lower limbs; the Arch Lich is thrashing with its whole body.
findings.replacement: The Arch Lich flailed its arms and legs in a frenzy, but the magic it fired collided with the heat surrounding me like a barrier and vanished before it could even reach me.
findings.source: 아크 리치가 발광하듯 손발을 흩뿌렸지만, 놈이 쏘아 보낸 마법은 내게 닿기도 전에 방어막처럼 주위를 둘러싼 열기와 부딪쳐 사라졌다.

summary: Several fidelity and register issues remain, including a changed theological quantity, lost military humor, altered willingness around Erasure, an omitted physical action, and localized terminology and prose problems.
